deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1966-67 preparatory notes for the 'Crystals' lectures (IHES, Nov.-Dec. 1967, written up as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' in Dix exposés). The setup is as follows. X/S is a scheme with its infinitesimal (or crystalline) topos, and Mod(X/S) is the category of modules on it. P^i_{(n)} are the sheaves of principal parts of the formal neighbourhoods of the diagonals X^{[i]} = (X/S)^{i+1}, which form a cosimplicial formal scheme P°. For a module M one has the 'linearization' Q^i[M] = lim_n P^i_{(n)} ⊗ M. This is a cosimplicial resolution, a Čech-Alexander type complex, and it computes H^*(X/S, M) as Zariski hypercohomology of ℓQ°[M].

The previous page extends this to bounded-below complexes M^· in D^+(X/S). One gets a bicomplex Q^*[M^·] whose total complex resolves M^·. The remark is that Q°[M^·] is the formalization of complexes of differential operators.

This page (§5) takes M^· ∈ D^+(X/S) and considers ℓQ°[M^·], a complex of pro-O_X-Modules with stratifications. Grothendieck states that knowing this complex recovers M^· in stages:
- first as a complex of additive sheaves;
- then the sheaves of sections and the stratifications;
- finally the O_X-structures on the M^·, recovered as conditions on extra structures on ℓQ°[M^·].
He recalls that these extra structures are not determined by the bare object ℓQ°[M^·] alone.

He then considers the cohomology sheaves H^i(ℓQ°[M^·]). He assumes their formation commutes with the cosimplicial base changes along P°. He says this will follow from flatness hypotheses. The next page gives these hypotheses: flatness of Q^0[M^·] and of its H^i, plus a 'differential flatness' of X/S, i.e. of X^{[1]} → X, e.g. X/S smooth.

The next page then draws the conclusions:
- (1) V^i = H^i are stratified O_X-modules, i.e. crystals.
- (2) Taking first the cohomology of the bicomplex in the direction of the differential operators of M^· yields the de Rham complexes of the stratified V^i.
- (3) Hence there is a spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p_dR(X, V^q) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X/S, M^·).

In modern terms: a complex of differential operators is linearized into a complex of crystals/D-modules. Under flatness its cohomology sheaves carry Gauss-Manin-type connections, and there is a Leray/Katz-Oda type spectral sequence from the de Rham cohomology of these crystals to the crystalline/infinitesimal cohomology of the complex.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. As written, the hypothesis that H^i commutes with cosimplicial base change is a sufficient condition stated without proof; the precise flatness criterion is left as '[critère : dégager]' on the next page.
The statement that M^· is recovered from ℓQ°[M^·] with its stratification is heuristic. Grothendieck himself warns that the O_X-structures need extra data beyond the object.

ideas.what: Linearization of a complex of differential operators / object of D^+(X/S) into a complex of pro-O_X-modules with stratification (crystals), from which the original complex is recoverable with extra structure
ideas.modern_name: Linearization functor L (complexes of differential operators ↔ complexes of D-modules / crystals); Čech-Alexander resolution
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals, 1968); developed by Berthelot (1974, Cohomologie cristalline, Ch. II/IV); Herrera-Lieberman; later Saito's equivalence for differential complexes
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Under flatness ('differential flatness' of X/S, e.g. smoothness), the cohomology sheaves of the linearized complex are stratified O_X-modules, i.e. crystals
ideas.modern_name: Gauss-Manin connection on relative cohomology sheaves (crystalline construction)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes

ideas.what: Spectral sequence from the de Rham cohomology of the stratified cohomology sheaves V^q to the cohomology of M^·
ideas.modern_name: Leray / Katz-Oda spectral sequence for crystalline-de Rham cohomology
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Crystals (Dix exposés) in the discussion of the Gauss-Manin connection

deep.surprise_reason: This is a preparatory sketch of material that appeared in Grothendieck's 1968 'Crystals' exposé and in Katz-Oda and Berthelot: linearization of complexes of differential operators, and Gauss-Manin crystals on cohomology sheaves with the associated spectral sequence. The only slightly unusual element is the loosely sketched 'reconstruction of M^· from its linearization' hierarchy, and that is heuristic and known in spirit.
transcription_corrections: '$\mathcal{C}^\circ[M^\cdot]$' throughout should read '$\ell Q^\circ[M^\cdot]$' (handwritten 'lQ°'), consistent with the later line '$\mathcal{H}^i(\ell Q^\circ[M^\cdot])$'.
Line 3: crossed-out '$\ell Q^\circ[$', then 'de (pro-$\mathcal{O}_X$-Modules) à stratifications'; the inserted 'X' is the subscript of $\mathcal{O}$.

'du point de vue des complexes additifs d'abord, ensuite [quant] aux faisceaux de sections, [et] stratifications, puis les $\mathcal{O}_X$-structures sur les $M^\cdot$ comme condition des structures extérieures données du $\ell Q^\circ[M^\cdot]$': the readings are plausible but uncertain.
'ne se répondront pas complètement par l'objet seul' is probably 'ne se reconstituent / ne se répercutent pas complètement par l'objet seul'; uncertain.
'$P^\circ \to P\mathcal{R}$' is uncertain. It likely denotes a morphism of cosimplicial (formal) schemes, a base change of the cosimplicial diagonal-neighbourhood object.
